strengths: Medical imaging is a real, not surface, match: BraTS 2020 multi-modal MRI pipeline with U-Net + VGG-16/19/ResNet-50 backbones, evaluated on Dice/IoU, with custom 3D volumetric batch-loading (Teesside Research Fellowship).
Healthcare document AI: fine-tuned DONUT on a custom medical billing dataset, 55% -> 93% validation accuracy (IIT Bombay). Closest thing to 'NLP for clinical text' in the profile.

Model deployment + optimization has genuine depth: TensorRT YOLO 5.2x speedup (56.7 -> 10.9 ms), ONNX/TFLite export for mobile, 8-bit quantization of TinyLlama at ~55% VRAM reduction with <1% accuracy loss.
Python / PyTorch / TensorFlow / Keras / HuggingFace backed by multiple independent projects, not one.
Git + GitLab + JupyterHub collaborative workflow used in a real lab setting (BARC).
real_gaps: Genomics / omics: zero evidence anywhere. No RNA-seq, WGS/WES, proteomics, transcriptomics, or bioinformatics pipelines. The JD lists genomics analysis as a core job duty, not just a preferred skill.
EHR / clinical data systems: zero. No Epic Clarity, no REDCap, no clinical informatics. Also named as a core duty.
Cloud + containers: zero. No AWS/Azure/GCP, no Docker, no Kubernetes. Profile's 'scale' experience is SLURM clusters and Jetson edge boards, and the JD explicitly names cloud infrastructure.

Production ML systems: deployments are research prototypes and edge demos. Nothing with monitoring, CI/CD, or on-call ownership. JD asks for 'research prototypes to production-ready systems in clinical environments'.
Healthcare regulatory standards (HIPAA, FDA SaMD): no exposure.
Classical/tabular ML: profile is deep learning end to end. EHR data mining is heavily gradient-boosting and survival-analysis territory, and there is no scikit-learn work to point at.
overstated_by_keywords: NumPy / pandas / scikit-learn — counted Adjacent, but none appear anywhere in the profile. They are almost certainly used, but there is no bullet to prove it.
'ML model deployment and production systems' — the deployment half is strong; the production-systems half is not evidenced.
'supervised/unsupervised learning' — supervised is well covered; unsupervised has no backing at all.
'Medical imaging' — real, but it rests on a single 6-week research fellowship rather than sustained work.
llm_analysis.reasoning: Justin clears every stated minimum qualification comfortably and exceeds them (M.S. vs Bachelor's, seven internships vs 'no prior experience required'). The gap is domain, not capability: the JD's actual day-to-day is genomics, EHR pipelines, and cloud infrastructure, and he has none of the three. For an Engineer I posting that explicitly requires no experience, that gap is the expected on-the-job learning curve rather than a disqualifier, and his BraTS medical-imaging fellowship gives him one legitimate foothold in the clinical domain. The realistic risk here is competition, not qualification.
